> Generated by BB-Discover for BB-Scan (Otomasyon 2). Do not submit reports from this brief alone.

## Chains & stack

- **Chains:** ethereum
- **Stack:** EVM smart contracts + web apps
- **Languages:** Solidity, NextJS

## Services to activate

Read `config/services.yaml` and `config/chains.yaml` in the orchestrator repo.

- git
- foundry
- rpc_provider
- block_explorer
- foundry_fork

### RPC/Explorer mapping (from config/chains.yaml)

- Ethereum RPC env var: `ALCHEMY_ETH_RPC` (fallback: `INFURA_ETH_RPC`)
- Explorer: Etherscan (`https://etherscan.io`), API env var: `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`
- Foundry fork note: use local fork testing only (`forge test --fork-url $ALCHEMY_ETH_RPC`), no live mainnet testing unless explicitly allowed.

## Scope (in-scope)

- ENS smart contracts in latest finalized mainnet release (`vx.x.x`).
- Eligible recognized deployments for testnet carve-out as defined by ENS rules.

## Out of scope — DO NOT REPORT

- `https://ens.dev` is out of scope.
- Website/application testnet and staging deployments are out of scope.
- Mainnet release candidates and pre-release builds are out of scope.
- Unrecognized testnet deployments are out of scope.

## Known issues — DUPLICATE RISK

- Malicious DAO can steal names using NameWrapper upgrade.
- Malicious DAO can reduce expiration of names.
- Namewrapper race condition allowing inappropriate fuse setting.
- Any unfixed vulnerabilities in prior audits are ineligible.
- Treat Sherlock/Cantina prior audit findings as duplicate-risk classes.

## Prohibited testing

- Any testing on mainnet or public testnet deployed code.
- Any testing with pricing oracles or third-party smart contracts.
- Any testing with third-party systems/apps/websites (browser extensions, SSO, ad networks).
- Denial-of-service or significant-traffic automated testing.
- Social engineering or phishing.
- Public disclosure of unpatched embargoed vulnerabilities.
- Respect Immunefi exclusion list, default prohibited activities, and Immunefi Rules.

## Submission rules

- PoC is required for all severities.
- Responsible publication category 3 (approval required).
- First valid disclosure only.
- Follow Immunefi VSC v2.3 and program-specific payout discretion language.

## Hunt hypotheses (top 3)

1. NameWrapper permission/fuse edge-cases around upgradeability and role assumptions.
2. Resolver/registry cross-contract state inconsistency enabling unauthorized resolution changes.
3. Reward-affecting logic flaws in release-version gating between finalized and pre-release deployments.

## Exploit surface focus

- Permissionless entry points in ENS registry/resolver/namewrapper flows.
- Integration boundaries (resolver plugins, offchain dependencies).
- Upgrade/proxy/admin paths (note admin-malicious assumptions are often discounted).
- Economic invariants around name ownership expiry and fuse semantics.

## Skills for BB-Scan

1. Obsidian + RAG preflight (`obsidian-web3`, `web3-bbp-rag`)
2. Pashov `x-ray` on in-scope contracts only
3. Pashov `solidity-auditor` on in-scope files only
4. Manual checklist sections 3–7 before any PoC

## Abort signals

Stop scan if:

- Matching `30-findings/` note with `status/duplicate` or `status/disputed`
- Known issue text matches suspected bug class
- Target is out-of-scope chain or contract list
